# Best pick: ESR 100W 6-in-1 Charging Station

The ESR 100W 6-in-1 is the only single unit in these results that charges a laptop, phone and watch together. It has:
- An Apple-certified MagSafe pad for the phone
- A dedicated Apple Watch charger
- An AirPods pad
- 2× USB-C and 1× USB-A ports for the laptop, all from one 100W GaN plug

**Price:** $164.99 list. With code PARTNER18 (18% off, expires 2026-12-31, last tested 2026-10-22) it's about $135.30. It was in stock when checked.

**Buy:** [ESR 100W 6-in-1 MagSafe + CryoBoost Station](https://dealectric.com/go/esr-100w-6-in-1-magsafe-cryoboost-station). This is an affiliate link, so Dealectric is paid if you buy, at no cost to you. (Source: [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/answers/best-desk-charging-station-laptop-phone-watch-2026-usb-c-laptop-power-delivery-3))

**Laptop power limit:** The full 100W only reaches one USB-C port when the wireless pads are idle. While the pads are charging, the laptop gets up to 65W, or 45W if the second USB-C port is also in use. That's fine for a MacBook Air-class laptop but marginal for a 14" or 16" MacBook Pro or other high-wattage laptops. The pads are also Apple-oriented, so this suits an iPhone and Apple Watch best.

# Alternatives

- **Strong laptop power, no watch charger:** The [Baseus Nomos 5-in-1](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-nomos-5-in-1-140w-qi2) ($149.99) delivers 140W on one USB-C port, enough for a 16" MacBook Pro. It has a Qi2 phone pad and a retractable 100W cable, but you'd plug your watch's charger into a spare port. It was sold out when checked, so confirm stock first. (Source: [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/answers/best-desk-charging-station-laptop-phone-watch-2026-usb-c-laptop-power-delivery-3))

- **Best wireless stand to pair with your own laptop charger:** WIRED's top 3-in-1 for iPhone, Apple Watch and AirPods is the Belkin 3-in-1 Qi2 Charging Stand (about $98, with a 15W phone pad). WIRED's budget pick is the ESR Qi2 3-in-1 (about $40 on sale). Both handle the phone and watch, and your laptop would keep its own charger. See the [WIRED guide](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-apple-3-in-1-wireless-chargers/) for links.

- **Wattage check:** One guide suggests summing your devices' fast-charge draw and adding about 20% headroom ([The Office Journal](https://www.theofficejournal.com/guide/best-charging-stations-for-multiple-devices-desk)).

Tell me which laptop and phone you use, and I can say whether the ESR's 65W-with-pads limit is enough or whether the Baseus or a separate setup makes more sense.
